name: Building a module for Portal Server
about: How a Portal Server module is built: layout, what the loader looks for, pages, intents, the house rules and code style. For agents and people writing modules.
text:
# Building a module for Portal Server

A module is part of the portal, not an app beside it: it runs inside the portal's process, is reached at /module/<name>/, uses the portal's users, page shell, toolbars, settings and intents, and keeps its data in the portal's data folder. Build on what exists; add a missing lever to the shared part (core built_ins) rather than a copy in the module.

## Layout
- `modules/<name>/<name>.py` - the module. The loader imports it and needs nothing else. Optional beside it: `requirements.txt` (pip names; installed at start, so bake them into the image for offline installs), more `.py` files it imports by path, `library/` (data it ships: faces, pipelines, contexts - JSON), `static/` only for files that may be public.
- Data: `data/<name>/` (the loader makes it; `env["data_dir"]`). Never write beside the code. Anything personal or setup-specific (names of people, machines, accounts, worlds) is data, never code or comments.
- A file named `DISABLED` in the folder keeps the module from loading without moving anything. A module that fails at load is left out and named; the portal still starts.

## The two names the loader looks for
- `router = APIRouter(redirect_slashes=False)` - mounted at /module/<name>, behind login.
- `MODULE_META = {"label", "icon" (an HTML code such as 📚), "description", "persistence": "user" | "public"}`.
- `def init_module(env: dict)` - called once with the portal's parts. Keep them in module globals. The ones used most: `env["tools"]["built_ins"]` (BI: TabManager, ChatManager, SettingsGroup / SettingField, FileManager, ShadowStore, ImageGallery ...), `env["templates"]` (Jinja), `env["templates"].env.globals["UI"]` (toolbar, modal, tab_bar ...), `env["InterfaceManager"]` (intents), `env["ws"]`, `env["data_dir"]`, `env["register_service"]` / `env["services"]` (call another module or tool by name, no load order), `env["register_startup"]` (an async function started with the server: background loops), `env["tools"]["aviary"]` (pipelines and AI: start runs, never call a model directly).

## A page
- `@router.get("/")` answers the whole page: `env["templates"].TemplateResponse(name="base.html", request=request, context={"request": request, "user": request.state.user, "nesting_level": 1, "shell_id": IM.branch_id, "content": ..., "extra_css": ..., "extra_script": ..., "toolbars": {...}})` - keyword names, always.
- Toolbars: `UI.toolbar(side="top"|"left"|"right", content=..., id=..., nesting_level=1, ...)`. Tabs: `BI.TabManager` (merge new default tabs into saved state and save, or existing users never see them).
- The page works on a phone: no px sizes (rem, %, vh, min()), tables whose first column wraps, nothing that only works on hover.

## Doing things: intents, not endpoints
- `IM = env["InterfaceManager"](nesting_level=1, db_path=f"{data_dir}/im_registry.db")`, then `IM.scripts["<name>_<verb>"] = [async handler(request, payload, imr)]`. Intent names are unique portal-wide: prefix them with the module's name.
- A button: hx-post to /im/in with `{"type": "<name>_<verb>", ...}` and `hx-swap="none"`; the handler answers with `imr.oob(html, element_id)` (inner HTML of that element) or `imr.raw(html)` (html that carries hx-swap-oob itself). A top-level <script> in an answer never runs: put scripts inside the swapped element.
- A repeated form key (a checkbox group) arrives as a list, a single one as a string. hx-vals on a control override the form's fields of the same name.
- Toolbar buttons use `pointerdown`, selects `change`. Vanilla JS and HTMX only; libraries from /static/js/.

## Rules of the house
- The owner is sovereign; every limit is an internal, settable decision. Anything that can be set has a setting (`BI.SettingsGroup` with `BI.SettingField`, extended in built_ins when a kind of field is missing); settings keep on change, never need buttons pressed in order.
- Stakes rule: never overwrite or delete data without the consent of everyone who values it. Free names (-2, -3) instead of replacing; confirm deletes; nothing pre-ticked in a delete list; changes to shared files go through proposals (ShadowStore) a person accepts.
- Picking files or folders is from a tree (FileManager's picker); typing a name is only an extra.
- The UI never waits: draw a placeholder at once and fill it when the answer comes (hx-trigger="load"). What is shown must be what happens; never truncate an error or status shown to a person.
- AI is a user like any other: what an AI may do in the module is a grant (scope service, check(user, thing, act)), not a special path.
- Fail fast: no try/except around things that must exist; catch only outside data or services, and show the error where the person is looking.
- Privacy and FOSS: say when something contacts an outside server or uses a non-free part, and how to turn it off.

## Code style (the maintainer's, required)
- Compact: one-line functions where readable, no single-use variables, no line-length wrapping, at most one `;` per line, `# --- Section ---` headers, new code next to related code.
- f-strings: one string, never split; an f-string whose body holds a quote character is triple-quoted. Python 3.11: no triple-quoted f-string inside another (build the inner part first).
- httpx: a plain timeout or all four of `httpx.Timeout(connect=, read=, write=, pool=)`.
- Comments describe the code for any reader, not the request that led to it. Write "-" not long dashes; emoji as HTML codes.
- Under 1000 lines a file: past that, move a group of functions into a file beside it.

## Before proposing a change
- Read the section being changed, and the shared parts it could use (core built_ins.py, main.py's registries) - much already exists.
- Propose the change with why, in small steps that can each be checked; say what was not checked.
